title: How Much Do Permanent Christmas Lights Cost in 2026?
body_markdown:
Permanent Christmas lights cost an average of $3,200 installed nationally in 2026, with basic single-color strands starting around $1,800 and full smart-control systems on larger or multi-story homes reaching $7,500 or more. That headline number usually excludes the cost of extra electrical work — a dedicated outlet or new circuit — which adds $150 to $500 depending on your panel's capacity and how far the wiring has to run.


**TL;DR**

- Permanent Christmas lights cost $1,800 to $7,500+ installed in 2026, averaging around $3,200 for a standard single-story home.
- Per linear foot, expect $28 to $45 installed depending on channel type, color count, and mounting.
- App-controlled multi-color systems cost more upfront but end the yearly install-and-removal labor of seasonal lights.
- Electrical upgrades such as a new outlet or circuit are rarely included and add $150 to $500.
- CleanGutters Lighting installs custom architectural roofline lighting across South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware.


## Why this matters

Most people asking how much do permanent Christmas lights cost are comparing it against paying a seasonal crew every November, or against doing it themselves on a ladder. That comparison only holds up if you know what is actually inside the quote — linear footage, channel count, and control hardware move the price far more than the brand name on the bulbs.

A $1,800 basic system and a $6,000 smart system both get called "permanent Christmas lights," but they solve different problems. Get the driver factors wrong and you either overpay for features you never touch or underbuy a system that cannot do multiple colors for Halloween, the Fourth of July, and December.

## How much do permanent Christmas lights cost in 2026?

Pricing breaks down by linear footage of roofline covered and the type of system installed. Here is how the tiers compare on a standard single-family home:

| System type | Typical installed cost (2026) | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Single-color, fixed strand | $1,800 – $3,000 | Homeowners who only decorate for winter holidays |
| Multi-color, app-controlled | $3,000 – $5,500 | Households wanting holiday, sports, and everyday color |
| Full smart system, large or multi-story | $5,500 – $7,500+ | Bigger homes, steep rooflines, complex trim |

Cost per linear foot runs roughly **$28 to $45 installed** in 2026. The low end reflects single-color aluminum channel on a simple ranch roofline. The high end reflects multi-story homes with dormers, gables, or long soffit runs that slow the install down.

### Single-color, fixed strand: $1,800–$3,000

One color, one channel, usually run on a basic timer or a single app zone. It covers standard fascia and roofline runs on a one-story home with straightforward trim. **Verdict: Buy** if you only want holiday-season lighting and will never need color changes.

### Multi-color, app-controlled: $3,000–$5,500

This tier adds RGB or RGBW bulbs and a controller that switches colors by app for different holidays, team colors, or everyday accent light. It is the tier most homeowners land on, because the install cost spreads across the whole year instead of six weeks in December. **Verdict: Buy** if you want the system earning its keep past the holidays.

### Full smart system, large or multi-story home: $5,500–$7,500+

Larger homes, steep pitches, and heavy architectural trim — dormers, bay windows, wraparound porches — need more linear footage, more mounting labor, and sometimes an added circuit. **Verdict: Buy** if your roofline complexity pushes total footage past what a standard quote assumes. Get it measured on site rather than estimated from a photo.



CleanGutters Lighting handles custom architectural [roofline lighting](https://cleangutterslighting.com/) alongside gutter guard installation and gutter cleaning across South Jersey, Eastern Pennsylvania, and Northern Delaware. That combination matters here: plenty of permanent lighting quotes climb after the crew finds the fascia or gutter behind the mounting line needs work first.

## Why permanent Christmas light cost varies

- **Linear footage of roofline** — the single biggest driver. More feet of fascia and trim means more channel, more bulbs, more labor hours.
- **Number of colors and channels** — single-color fixed strands cost less than multi-zone RGB systems that need a dedicated controller.
- **Mounting method** — fascia-channel mounting is faster than integrated soffit or recessed installs, which need precise fitting.
- **Home height and access** — second and third stories, steep pitches, and landscaping that blocks ladder placement all add labor time.
- **Electrical capacity** — homes needing a new outlet or dedicated circuit add $150 to $500, usually quoted separately from the lighting itself.
- **Existing gutter and fascia condition** — damaged fascia or sagging gutter behind the mounting line needs repair before lighting installs cleanly, and that is its own line item.

## Is permanent Christmas lighting cheaper than hiring seasonal installers every year?

Permanent Christmas lights typically break even against seasonal hiring within 2 to 4 seasons in 2026, because a seasonal crew bills you every single year while a permanent system is a one-time installed cost. The math shifts on two variables: what you were already paying per season, and how many more years you plan to stay in the house.

### Do permanent Christmas lights add resale value?

Permanent roofline lighting is treated as a feature buyers notice rather than a separately appraised value add, much like landscape lighting. Call it a livability upgrade in 2026, not a guaranteed return at closing.

### How long does a permanent Christmas light installation take?

Most single-story homes take one full day. Larger or multi-story homes with complex trim run to two days, driven by the same linear-footage and access factors that set the price.

## FAQ


**How much do permanent Christmas lights cost per linear foot?**

Permanent Christmas lights cost roughly $28 to $45 per linear foot installed in 2026. The low end applies to single-color systems on simple rooflines; the high end applies to multi-color systems on complex trim.

**What is the average cost of permanent Christmas lights in 2026?**

The average installed cost is about $3,200 in 2026, with a full range of $1,800 to $7,500 or more. Home size and roofline complexity explain most of that spread.

**Are permanent Christmas lights worth it compared to seasonal installation?**

Permanent Christmas lights usually pay for themselves within 2 to 4 seasons versus hiring a crew each year. After break-even, ongoing cost is close to zero apart from occasional bulb replacement.

**What is included in a permanent Christmas light installation quote?**

A standard quote covers lighting channel, bulbs, mounting hardware, and labor for the measured linear footage. Electrical upgrades such as a new outlet or circuit are quoted separately and add $150 to $500.

**Can permanent Christmas lights be used year-round for other colors?**

Multi-color app-controlled systems switch colors for any holiday or occasion year-round. Single-color fixed strands are locked to whatever color was installed.

**Do permanent lights need gutter or fascia repair first?**

If the fascia or gutter behind the mounting channel is damaged or sagging, that repair has to happen before the lighting installs cleanly. Have the roofline inspected before you collect lighting quotes.

**How long does it take to install permanent Christmas lights?**

Most single-story homes take one day. Larger or multi-story homes with complex trim take two days, depending on linear footage and ladder access.

**Is a dedicated circuit required for permanent Christmas lights?**

Not always, but homes without a suitable exterior outlet near the control point need one added. That electrical work runs $150 to $500 on top of the lighting quote.


## One last thing

The line item most homeowners miss when comparing 2026 quotes for permanent Christmas lights is not the lighting at all — it is the condition of the fascia and gutter behind the mounting channel. A gutter and fascia check before you accept a lighting quote is the cheapest way to avoid an unplanned add-on discovered on install day.
